newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips ease, SAX index falls 4.67 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips ease, SAX index falls 4.67 pts.

text.p: Losses to several blue chips shares pushed the Bratslava Stock Exchange's SAX index down 4.67 points to 202.55 on Friday, closing out another week of listless activity.
Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB lost 150 crowns to close at 1,600, with its average price -- used for calculating the index -- down 7.57 percent.
Brokers said there was no stable price for VUB shares at the moment, though a further decline in near future in the issue is expected.
"VUB may be (also) affected by the overall downward trend on the market...the price may even fall to 1,000 crowns, which would be more or less a realistic price," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.

Steel maker VSZ closed up one crown at 620, but its average price eased by 5.85 percent. Brokers still consider VSZ as a good share, saying the issue only suffered by the lethargic mood on the market.
Oil and gas storage firm Nafta closed up 55 at 2,025, but brokers said the overall volume of 10,000 shares was a single block deal.
Oil refiner Slovnaft did not trade on Friday.
Overall volume increased to 781,328 shares, from 164,329 shares traded on Thursday. Turnover rose to 601.50 million crowns, from 108.33 million on Thursday.
